snapshot.algorithm: sha256(filename + NUL + bytes + NUL, sorted by filename)

schema.name: feature_observations
schema.sql:
CREATE TABLE feature_observations (
        id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        scan_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES world_scans(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
        feature_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES world_features(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
        status TEXT,
        completion_ratio REAL,
        condition_score REAL,
        expected_blocks INTEGER,
        observed_blocks INTEGER,
        details_json TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
        observed_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
        UNIQUE (scan_id, feature_id)
      )

schema.name: world_features
schema.sql:
CREATE TABLE world_features (
        id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        project_id TEXT NOT NULL,
        external_id TEXT,
        parent_id TEXT REFERENCES world_features(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
        world TEXT NOT NULL,
        name TEXT NOT NULL,
        kind TEXT NOT NULL,
        status TEXT NOT NULL,
        geometry_json TEXT NOT NULL,
        min_x REAL NOT NULL,
        max_x REAL NOT NULL,
        min_z REAL NOT NULL,
        max_z REAL NOT NULL,
        source TEXT NOT NULL,
        source_ref TEXT,
        confidence REAL,
        completion_ratio REAL,
        condition_score REAL,
        tags_json TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
        attributes_json TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
        observed_at INTEGER,
        revision INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
        created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
        updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
        UNIQUE (project_id, external_id)
      )

schema.name: world_scans
schema.sql:
CREATE TABLE world_scans (
        id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        project_id TEXT NOT NULL,
        world TEXT NOT NULL,
        method TEXT NOT NULL,
        status TEXT NOT NULL,
        bounds_json TEXT,
        observer TEXT,
        snapshot_ref TEXT,
        summary_json TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
        error TEXT,
        started_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
        completed_at INTEGER
      )

schema.name: buildings
schema.sql:

schema.name: disasters

schema.name: relationships
schema.sql:
CREATE TABLE relationships (

schema.name: residents
schema.sql:
CREATE TABLE residents (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    town_id TEXT REFERENCES towns(id),

    joined_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
    current_role TEXT,
    status TEXT,
    UNIQUE (town_id, bot_name)
  )

schema.name: style_observations
schema.sql:
CREATE TABLE style_observations (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    town_id TEXT REFERENCES towns(id),
    building_id TEXT REFERENCES buildings(id),
    palette_json TEXT,
    recorded_at INTEGER,
    included INTEGER DEFAULT 1
  )

schema.name: towns
schema.sql:
CREATE TABLE towns (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT NOT NULL,
    founded_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
    capital_x INTEGER,
    capital_y INTEGER,
    capital_z INTEGER,
    tier TEXT CHECK (tier IN ('founding','village','town')),
    status TEXT CHECK (status IN ('active','dormant','abandoned')),
    population_target INTEGER,
    alliance_state TEXT,
    parent_town_id TEXT,
    style_seed TEXT,
    config_json TEXT,
    paused INTEGER DEFAULT 0
  )

worldFeature.projectId: Top-level authored area or project owning the object.
worldFeature.externalId: Stable human-authored ID, unique within a project.
worldFeature.parentId: Optional world_features.id of the containing object.
worldFeature.name: Human-readable object name.
worldFeature.kind: Finite object class: property, district, building, room, road, driveway, parking, sidewalk, fence, lighting, landscape, utility, landmark, or custom.
worldFeature.geometry: Point, axis-aligned bounds, path, or polygon in world coordinates.
worldFeature.bounds: Indexed X/Z envelope derived from geometry for spatial queries.
worldFeature.source: How the record entered the catalog.
worldFeature.sourceRef: Path or external reference supporting the record.
worldFeature.attributes: Project-specific JSON evidence, program, QA, and provenance.
worldFeature.observedAt: Epoch-ms time of the latest associated observation.

worldScan.method: region_snapshot, bot_terrain, rcon, manual, manifest_import, or plugin_event.
worldScan.observer: Tool or actor performing the survey.

notes: world-map.db is the cross-project as-built catalog and contains geometry, hierarchy, status, provenance, QA attributes, scans, and observations.
town.db is the Town Builder operational database for governed settlements; it is not a replacement for the cross-project catalog.
The data/ directory also contains JSON-backed operational stores. Their file inventory is included without reproducing logs, embeddings, or token-ledger contents.

The staged building floor-plan atlas uses 2 immutable sources; use artifacts[].sourceSnapshot; C01-PUBLIC-PORTAL-RECESSED-PHASE2 at snapshot 4fca1ff3c40ae9c24c9338483b0780678aa5966bb570a642f0d0277885331a2b.

The catalog snapshot, current surface maps, and new perspective captures retain separate provenance. Do not relabel an inherited floor plan with the catalog snapshot; use the per-artifact source record.
